plain.Space Weather Nowcast: Live readings from a spacecraft about 1.5 million km toward the Sun, turned into a countdown for when that solar wind reaches Earth, and a map of the aurora's reach compared with Syracuse.
plain.Live Earthquake Statistics: Every earthquake the US Geological Survey recorded this week, refreshed every minute. It tests a classic law about how much rarer big quakes are, and logs each time the catalog quietly corrects itself.
plain.Order Book Microstructure: A live copy of a Bitcoin exchange's order book, rebuilt from more than a hundred updates a second and checked against the exchange's own fingerprint after every single one.
plain.Wikipedia Edit Stream: Every edit to Wikipedia and its sister sites, live, about 30 a second. The page counts them two ways at once, exactly and with memory saving shortcuts, so you can watch how far off the shortcuts drift.
plain.Replicating Dr. GRPO: I re-ran a 2025 paper about training AI models to reason. Its accuracy result held up. Its two claims about answer length came out the other way, in one training run.
plain.Tool Dependency Graph: AI assistants fail when they call tools in the wrong order. I worked out the right order for 1,391 tools using nothing but each tool's written spec.
plain.Distributed ViT on CIFAR-10: I split one model's training across two GPUs and nearly doubled the speed. Switching to a smaller number format shrank the gain to 1.15x, and I traced the slowdown to the machine's 4 CPUs.
plain.ZTF Transient Pipeline: A sky survey telescope sends alerts whenever something in the sky changes. I replayed one real night of them, 27,378 alerts, through a pipeline that streams them, scores a 500 alert sample, and stores the results.
plain.Groundwork: A test bench for AI that answers questions. It checks whether the system finds the right passage, admits when it does not know, and resists people trying to trick it.
plain.Replicating BEIR: I rebuilt a well known search benchmark from scratch. All six published numbers reproduced, four of them exactly. One was off at first because a library quietly cut every document short, and I tracked that down.
plain.JMA Wireless: At a maker of 5G equipment, a robot assembly line ran 97% of the time but hit only 46% of its weekly target. My team showed it was waiting on parts, not broken.
plain.ShopFloor AI: Predicts which factory machines are about to fail, streams live production numbers, and answers questions from maintenance manuals, all running as seven connected services.
plain.handoff: Automated systems often wait forever for a person to approve something. Here every request has a deadline, and the rules say what happens if nobody answers: escalate, use a safer option, drop it, or freeze.
plain.comms-agent: An AI agent that sorts media mentions about a brand, stops so a person can fix the ones it is unsure of, and only then writes its report. Tested on sample data.
plain.Project Mark: I built data analysis puzzles with hidden traps and verified answers, to see whether top AI models fall for them. On the clean versions, they did not.
plain.media-pulse: Sorts news mentions by topic and mood, and sends the uncertain ones to a person. With that review, topic accuracy rises from 88% to 96% on sample data.
plain.Multi Horizon Geomagnetic Kp Index Predi: Forecasts geomagnetic storms, the space weather behind the northern lights, from solar wind data. One hour ahead, its error is 45% lower than guessing the average.
plain.The Perfect Lap: Predicts when a Formula 1 team will make its first pit stop. On average it is about 3 laps off.
plain.Managing July Energy Demand Under a Warm: If July were 5°C hotter, my model says peak home energy use would rise about 25%. Nudging thermostats up 1°C during peak hours would win back about 9%.
plain.Challenging \"Wealth Equals Health\": Across 180+ countries, years of schooling predict child mortality as strongly as income does, with a tighter fit. Income matters, but it is not the first lever funders should pull.
plain.Uber Data Engineering Pipeline: Takes raw New York City taxi trip data and builds it into clean, connected tables in Google BigQuery, ready for a dashboard.
plain.Travel Itinerary Management System: A trip planning database that rejects bad data on its own, like negative prices or zero length activities, and assembles a whole itinerary in one call.
plain.Digit Recognition Neural Network from Sc: A neural network that reads handwritten digits, written without any AI library so every step is visible. It gets 94% right.
plain.Real Time Big Data Inflow: A review of 12+ studies on where to process streaming data: in a distant cloud, or closer to where it is produced. For suitable workloads the comparison puts the cut in delay at 40 to 60%.

jobs.Research Assistant, Gravity Spy 2.0: LIGO listens for colliding black holes, and noise glitches get in the way. I help find which parts of the detector cause them, working from 276,000+ volunteer classifications.
jobs.Lean Six Sigma Project Lead: I led a four person team at JMA Wireless that found why a robot line missed its targets, and gave managers numbers they could finally compare across lines.
jobs.Cybersecurity Teaching Assistant: I taught hands on security labs: breaking into deliberately weak machines, then reading the same evidence the way a defender would.
jobs.Data and Product Analyst Intern: I dug through customer data at a software company to find which features people used, ignored, and paid for.
